catalog.typeLabDesc: Five directions to compare in context
catalog.colorLabDesc: Six natural palettes with WCAG contrast
lab.palette.actual.name: Current
lab.palette.actual.tagline: Forest green: the palette already in the app
lab.palette.actual.summary: The current deep green, with bluish ink and warm paper. A baseline for measuring how much each proposal changes.
lab.palette.actual.notes.0: An established identity and strong contrast in text and buttons.
lab.palette.actual.notes.1: Keeping it requires no token migration.
lab.palette.actual.watchOut.0: Bluish ink (H 257) makes the overall palette feel cooler.
lab.palette.actual.watchOut.1: Green and ochre do not share a consistent ramp structure.
lab.palette.dehesa.name: Verde dehesa
lab.palette.dehesa.tagline: The same forest, with warm ink and paper
lab.palette.dehesa.summary: Refines the current palette: a slightly deeper green, warm paper and green-black ink. The lowest-risk evolution.
lab.palette.dehesa.notes.0: Keeps the recognisable green and increases contrast.
lab.palette.dehesa.notes.1: Green ink connects text and brand; ochre remains for notices.
lab.palette.dehesa.watchOut.0: The change is subtle; unsuitable for a major visual shift.
lab.palette.dehesa.watchOut.1: Review the cool neutral colours still present in components.
lab.palette.olivar.name: Olivar y cal
lab.palette.olivar.summary: A dry Mediterranean landscape: olive trees, limestone and terracotta. The earthiest, most archaeological proposal.
lab.palette.olivar.notes.0: Olive and clay suggest nature and heritage.
lab.palette.olivar.notes.1: The limestone background feels warm without yellowing; warm accents work for notices and maps.
lab.palette.olivar.watchOut.0: Olive green feels less energetic than forest green; test calls to action.
lab.palette.olivar.watchOut.1: Existing cool greys stand out; neutral colours need tokens.
lab.palette.turia.name: Riu Turia
lab.palette.turia.summary: Deep watery teal, golden reeds and a pale sky background. Fresh, clean and very legible.
lab.palette.turia.notes.0: Distinguishes the map and waterside routes; golden reed tones add warmth.
lab.palette.turia.notes.1: Blue-green ink fits the overall palette.
lab.palette.turia.watchOut.0: May feel more like a riverside park than a botanical guide.
lab.palette.turia.watchOut.1: Blue competes with the map’s location marker; keep their roles separate.
lab.palette.azahar.name: Azahar
lab.palette.azahar.summary: Leaf green with orange blossom and saffron tones. The most Valencian and lively proposal, aimed at families and school groups.
lab.palette.azahar.notes.0: Orange energises calls to action and notices; green remains the brand colour.
lab.palette.azahar.notes.1: Connects with Valencia’s citrus identity without becoming a cliché.
lab.palette.azahar.watchOut.0: Orange needs green or ink nearby to avoid looking like an alert.
lab.palette.azahar.watchOut.1: Do not put white text on orange; use `warmStrong` instead.
lab.palette.piedra.name: Piedra y musgo
lab.palette.piedra.summary: Low saturation, stone and moss tones. The most restrained, heritage-focused proposal, giving photos and content prominence.
lab.palette.piedra.notes.0: Content and photos become more prominent.
lab.palette.piedra.notes.1: Moss and clay suggest natural materials; a good basis for cultural routes.
lab.palette.piedra.watchOut.0: Less sense of living nature; it may feel dull.
lab.palette.piedra.watchOut.1: Low moss contrast needs care with small text.
lab.direction.actual.name: Previous (Inter)
lab.direction.actual.tagline: The app’s baseline before the decision
lab.direction.actual.summary: The app declares Inter in its token but does not load the font, so most devices display system-ui. Here it is loaded for an accurate comparison.
lab.direction.actual.notes.0: The scale already in `src/index.css`; used as a baseline.
lab.direction.actual.notes.1: Choosing it only requires loading Inter and enlarging body and caption text.
lab.direction.actual.watchOut.0: 15 px body and 11.5 px captions are below comfortable sizes for a broad audience.
lab.direction.actual.watchOut.1: Headings lack a distinct voice; green carries all the personality.
lab.direction.guia.name: Guía de campo
lab.direction.guia.tagline: Organic serif headings, Inter for everything else
lab.direction.guia.summary: Fraunces evokes a botanical guide and field notebook; Inter keeps the interface familiar. The most character with the least risk.
lab.direction.guia.notes.0: Fraunces has optical axes and a touch of wonk, making it warm without being decorative.
lab.direction.guia.notes.1: Body text stays in Inter: the interface is familiar and reading gains 1 px.
lab.direction.guia.notes.2: Scientific names can be italic in body text; headings remain upright.
lab.direction.guia.watchOut.0: Do not use Fraunces below 20 px; it loses definition at small sizes.
lab.direction.guia.watchOut.1: Negative serif tracking should be minimal; never -0.02em.
lab.direction.cuaderno.name: Cuaderno botánico
lab.direction.cuaderno.tagline: Alegreya for reading, Alegreya Sans for controls
lab.direction.cuaderno.summary: A humanist superfamily with calligraphic roots. Prose feels like a herbarium story while controls stay clear. The most editorial and classically natural option.
lab.direction.cuaderno.notes.0: Alegreya and Alegreya Sans share a structure: cohesion without repeating the same voice.
lab.direction.cuaderno.notes.1: The serif needs 16.5 px and 1.6 line height for long paragraphs; the sans keeps the interface substantial.
lab.direction.cuaderno.notes.2: Fits cultural routes, species cards and herbarium texts.
lab.direction.cuaderno.watchOut.0: More classical and less app-like; test forms, buttons and bottom navigation.
lab.direction.cuaderno.watchOut.1: Keep Alegreya out of small labels; use the Sans instead.
lab.direction.sendero.name: Sendero cercano
lab.direction.sendero.summary: Bricolage Grotesque has soft terminals and a humanist touch; Nunito Sans softens reading. It evokes nature centres, families and school groups.
lab.direction.sendero.notes.0: The friendliest, least academic direction; suitable for families and schools.
lab.direction.sendero.notes.1: Nunito Sans remains legible in small sizes and controls.
lab.direction.sendero.watchOut.0: May feel more civic than botanical; green and photos must convey nature.
lab.direction.sendero.watchOut.1: Avoid extreme Bricolage weights; 500–700 is enough.
lab.direction.todos.name: Guía para todos
lab.direction.todos.tagline: Literata for reading, Atkinson for finding your way
lab.direction.todos.summary: The chosen direction. Literata is designed for reading; Atkinson Hyperlegible for distinguishing letters. It best brings nature to everyone while retaining warmth.
lab.direction.todos.notes.0: Atkinson distinguishes easily confused letters and numbers; ideal for buttons, figures and labels.
lab.direction.todos.notes.1: Literata gives a book-like reading experience without feeling academic.
lab.direction.todos.notes.2: The most inclusive of the five, with a public-service character.
lab.direction.todos.watchOut.0: Atkinson is distinctive; reserve it for interface and data rather than headings.
lab.direction.todos.watchOut.1: Test hierarchy and weights so the combination does not feel like two apps.
lab.sampleShort: A subtropical tree with violet flowers. In Valencia it shades avenues and gardens from late spring.
lab.sampleLong: A subtropical tree with violet flowers. In Valencia it shades avenues and gardens from late spring. Its bipinnate leaves resemble a fern and its flowering lasts a few weeks.
lab.sampleCaption: A subtropical tree with violet flowers, shading avenues and gardens.
lab.surfaceDesc: Secondary surface for panels, empty states and subtle groupings.
lab.colorIntro: The chosen direction is Verde dehesa: the same forest with warm ink and paper. The other five remain as references: Olivar y cal (Mediterranean), Riu Turia (fresh), Azahar (Valencian), Piedra y musgo (restrained) and the previous palette.
lab.colorFooter: Colours in OKLCH: each ramp keeps its hue and adjusts lightness and chroma. Hex values are the sRGB equivalents for labels and contrast calculations. The app uses the tokens in
lab.readingTitle: A guide to read on your phone
lab.readingBody: The card combines the scientific name with a brief explanation and an interesting fact. The text should fit a column of about 45 characters so the eye can easily find the next line.
lab.readingScientificAfter: is italicised, as botanical nomenclature requires; buttons and labels are not.
lab.readingSmall: Small text for captions, sources and help.
lab.typeIntro: The chosen direction is Guía para todos: Literata for headings and reading, Atkinson Hyperlegible for the interface. The other directions remain as references for ideas that were set aside or may be revisited.
